parts.text:
37 Four identical resistors are connected in a circuit, as shown.
30 V
X
Y
The battery has negligible internal resistance and an e.m.f. of 30 V.
What is the potential difference between the two points X and Y?
A
6.0 V
B
15 V
C
20 V
D
24 V

hints: Notice which resistors lie directly between X and Y: two identical resistors in series, so that section has resistance $2R$.
Notice the other section in the same loop: two identical resistors in parallel, so that section has resistance $R/2$ and the total is $2.5R$.
Use the same loop current through $2R$ and $R/2$ to compare shares of the 30 V e.m.f., then find $I \times 2R$ for X to Y.
walkthrough: Identify the loop: starting from the 30 V battery, current passes through the parallel pair then through Y to X via the two series resistors back to the battery.
Let each resistor be $R$. The X-Y section is two in series, so $R_{XY} = R + R = 2R$. The other section is two in parallel, so $R_{p} = R/2$.
Total resistance is $R_{total} = 2R + R/2 = 2.5R$. With negligible internal resistance, loop current is $I = 30 / 2.5R = 12/R$.
Potential difference between X and Y is the p.d. across $R_{XY}$: $V_{XY} = I \times 2R = (12/R) \times 2R = 24 \text{ V}$.
The larger resistance takes the larger share of 30 V, so 24 V across X-Y and 6 V across the parallel pair is consistent. This is option D.

A.explanation: Too small - this would be the p.d. across only half of one $R$ resistor, not across the two in series between X and Y.

B.explanation: This assumes the 30 V splits equally, ignoring that the parallel pair of $R$ has much less resistance than the series pair of $R$ between X and Y.

C.explanation: This is the p.d. across the parallel combination if miscalculated, not the larger share across the $2R$ section between X and Y.

D.explanation: The two resistors between X and Y take the major share of the 30 V because their $2R$ exceeds the $R/2$ of the parallel pair, giving 24 V.
